subject: StratusLane production: sustained 429s, latency spike & quota intervention request
messages:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@stratuslane.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratuslane.com
Date: 2028-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production drop: sustained 429s & latency from 10/18 08:45 PDT

Grace —

We're seeing a sustained spike in 429s and end-to-end latency starting ~08:45 PDT. Our service calls to your text-generation endpoint are failing intermittently and throughput has dropped by ~40% over the last 30m. This is impacting our customer-facing real-time features (session timeouts).

Quick facts:
- First observed: 2028-10-18 08:45 PDT
- Error: HTTP 429 + 504 latency spikes
- Impact: 40% throughput degradation, multiple user sessions dropped

I've attached a short sample of the request IDs and the traffic CSV with timestamps. Can you confirm whether any quota or burst policy change is being rolled out now? We need an immediate temporary relief path (quota increase or override) and an ETA on a root cause.

Please escalate if needed — this is on our critical path for the morning's release.

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Head of Platform, StratusLane
ethan.brooks@stratuslane.com

Attachments: stratuslane-429-sample-logs.txt, ingress-traffic-20281018.csv

Hi Ethan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm pulling Marissa (ops) and Sean (AM) into triage now.

Immediate plan:

- Marissa / Ops to confirm whether any global burst policy or routing change caused this.
- Sean will keep your team in the loop on the customer side and coordinate the exec thread if needed.

Can you confirm the most important endpoints (model & route) and whether you were running any heavy promotion/ingest at 08:30–09:00?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production drop: sustained 429s & latency from 10/18 08:45 PDT

Team —

Initial ops read: we see a large burst from StratusLane's tenant key starting 08:43. The traffic pattern matches a client-side retry storm combined with a tenant burst window that was sized conservatively. Summary so far:

- Observation: simultaneous increase in short-lived concurrent connections + repeated retries for timed-out tokens.
- Root candidate: tenant burst credit pool exhausted, failover to global safety valve causing per-request 429s and increased queueing (latency).
- Recent changes: none deployed to rate-limiter code this morning; however, a scheduled rebalancing job (traffic gating) finished at 08:30 and may have changed effective burst windows for some tenant cohorts.

Immediate actions I've kicked off:
1) Temporary tenant override: +60% burst credits for 2 hours (in progress).
2) Disable the scheduled rebalancing task for the impacted cohort while we validate (rollback queued).
3) Collect full KV cache / request-id logs and upload to drive (link below).
4) Ops will run a targeted replay with sanitized request IDs to confirm reproducer.

Attachments: redwood-temporary-override.pdf (policy snapshot)
Related link: https://redwood.app/dashboards/SL-451-traffic

I'm keeping Neha in the loop in case we need an exec-level decision (credits or SLA exception). Will update in 15–20m.

—Marissa
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production drop: sustained 429s & latency from 10/18 08:45 PDT

Ethan —

Quick customer-facing update: we've applied a temporary tenant override (+60% burst credits for 2 hours) to StratusLane and disabled the rebalancing job for the impacted cohort. Ops is replaying sanitized traffic now to validate behavior. Expected immediate impact: throughput should regain most traffic within ~5–10 minutes; we'll monitor.

Next steps (we propose):
- 2hr override in place; if stable, we'll step down to a 24hr elevated window while we tune the burst policy for your workload.
- Post-incident: joint postmortem and a recommended change to your client retry backoff defaults.

If you want to bring in your CTO/VP for an exec call, we can set up a 30m bridge — Marissa and Neha will join.

Thanks,
Grace
